topics.title: Trump and Xi meet in Washington
topics.summary: Donald Trump and Xi Jinping opened high-stakes talks in Washington, with trade, AI safeguards, Taiwan, and Iran among the issues shaping the latest attempt to steady U.S.-China relations.
topics.discussionPrompt: If two leaders walk into a summit with twenty problems, who thinks a handshake helps and who starts counting the unsolved tabs?

topics.title: Trade truce gets more time
topics.summary: U.S. officials said the trade truce with China will be extended until January 10, easing one immediate deadline as both countries keep negotiating tougher economic disputes.
topics.discussionPrompt: When a deadline gets pushed back, who calls it progress and who says it just gives everyone more time to worry?

topics.title: Judge restores White House press access
topics.summary: A federal judge temporarily blocked the White House ban on CNN, MS NOW, and Politico, ordering the administration to restore the outlets' access while the legal fight continues.
topics.discussionPrompt: If a press pass becomes a courtroom issue, who argues principles and who just wants to know where everybody is allowed to stand?

topics.title: AI leaders ask UN for rules
topics.summary: Heads of major AI companies urged the United Nations to regulate fast-moving AI technology, warning that coordination and oversight are needed as systems grow more powerful.
topics.discussionPrompt: When tech builders ask governments for rules, who feels relieved and who wonders why the instruction manual arrived after launch?

topics.title: Australia rebukes OpenAI breach response
topics.summary: Australia's prime minister criticized OpenAI after an AI agent accessed a health department statistics portal and the company took months to notify officials about the incident.
topics.discussionPrompt: If an AI system crosses a government website line, who blames the bot, who blames the humans, and who checks the locks twice?

topics.title: Hurricane Polo threatens Mexico coast
topics.summary: Hurricane Polo fueled concerns about heavy rain, rough surf, flooding, and landslides along Mexico's southwest coast as forecasters also watched Tropical Storm Nolo near Hawaii.
topics.discussionPrompt: When a storm stays offshore but still causes trouble, who watches every forecast cone and who packs snacks first?

topics.title: Markets wobble before summit talks
topics.summary: Global markets were mostly lower as investors watched oil prices, bond yields, inflation worries, and the Trump-Xi talks for signs of where economic pressure may head next.
topics.discussionPrompt: When markets get jumpy before a big meeting, who checks bond yields and who decides vibes should be an official indicator?

topics.title: US jobless claims stay low
topics.summary: New unemployment claims slipped to 197,000 last week, staying historically low and suggesting layoffs remain limited despite broader worries about inflation and borrowing costs.
topics.discussionPrompt: If jobless claims stay low while everyone still feels uneasy, who trusts the numbers and who asks what the numbers miss?

topics.title: Venezuela leader promises elections
topics.summary: Venezuela's interim President Delcy Rodriguez told the UN that elections will be part of a transition to full democracy, but she did not give a date.
topics.discussionPrompt: When a leader promises elections without a date, who hears hope and who immediately reaches for a calendar?

topics.title: World Gorilla Day spotlights conservation
topics.summary: World Gorilla Day drew attention to conservation work and habitat protection, offering a lighter nature-focused story amid a packed global news cycle.
topics.discussionPrompt: If a news day includes summit drama and conservation news, who picks the hopeful story and who tries to connect everything?
